cards.subject: Authorisation
says: asks the issuer to approve a payment and hold the funds
returns an approval or a decline code
does not by itself move money to the merchant
cards.use: want to confirm a card can pay before you ship goods
not: transfers the money to the merchant's bank at once

cards.subject: Capture
says: turns an approved authorisation into a request for the money
has to follow the authorisation within an allowed window
is the step after which the funds are due to be settled
cards.use: have shipped the goods and want to take the held money
not: can be done at any time after authorisation with no limit

cards.subject: A void
says: cancels an authorisation before it is captured
releases the hold on the cardholder's funds
means no money was ever taken
cards.use: need to cancel an order that has not been captured yet
not: returns money that has already been captured and settled

cards.subject: A refund
says: returns money to the customer after a payment was captured
is linked to the original payment
can cover only part of the original amount
cards.use: need to give back part of a payment that was already taken
not: is the same thing as a chargeback

cards.subject: A chargeback
says: is a dispute the cardholder raises with their own issuer
pulls the disputed amount back from the merchant while it is decided
gives the merchant a deadline to answer with evidence
cards.use: see a customer dispute a charge through their bank
not: is started by the merchant to reverse a sale

cards.subject: Settlement
says: moves captured funds towards the merchant in batches
happens after capture rather than at the same moment
is what eventually produces a payout to the bank
cards.use: want to know when captured money turns into money in the bank
not: happens at the same instant as authorisation

cards.subject: 3-D Secure
says: adds a cardholder authentication step such as a bank app prompt
can move liability for some fraud disputes to the issuer
may send the customer away from the checkout for a moment
cards.use: want an extra check that the real cardholder is paying online
not: removes the need for an authorisation request

cards.subject: A partial capture
says: takes less than the authorised total
is typical when only part of an order ships
can leave the rest of the hold to lapse or be released
cards.use: ship only part of an order that was authorised
not: voids the whole authorisation

cards.subject: Representment
says: is the merchant's evidence submission contesting a chargeback
travels back through the acquirer to the issuer
is decided by the issuer or card network, not by the merchant
cards.use: want to contest a dispute with proof of delivery
not: is a second authorisation sent to the issuer

cards.subject: Authorisation expiry
says: lapses a hold that is not captured in time
frees the held funds back to the cardholder
means a late capture needs a fresh authorisation
cards.use: find that goods ship long after the original approval
not: extends itself every time the order is edited

cards.subject: A decline code
says: tells the integrator why the issuer refused a payment
separates failures worth retrying from permanent ones
should be mapped to a customer-friendly message rather than shown raw
cards.use: must decide whether to retry a failed card payment
not: always means the card was stolen

cards.subject: A payment service provider
says: gives merchants one integration for several payment methods
handles the connections to acquirers and card networks
usually offers an API and a dashboard
cards.use: want to accept payments without building bank connections yourself
not: is the bank that issued the cardholder's card

cards.subject: An issuer
says: is the bank that gave the cardholder their card
decides whether to approve an authorisation
receives the chargeback request from its cardholder
cards.use: ask which party approves or declines the cardholder's payment
not: holds the merchant's account for receiving card funds

cards.subject: An acquirer
says: holds the merchant's account for receiving card funds
passes the merchant's transactions towards the card network
is the merchant's side of a card payment
cards.use: ask which bank receives the merchant's card money
not: decides whether the cardholder has enough funds

cards.subject: A card network
says: routes messages between acquirer and issuer
sets the rules that participants follow, including dispute rules
does not normally lend the money or hold the cardholder's account
cards.use: need the rails that connect both banks in a card payment
not: is the merchant's bank

cards.subject: A payment gateway
says: securely passes payment details from checkout to the processor
plays the online role of a physical card terminal
does not itself hold the merchant's funds
cards.use: need the secure link between a web checkout and the processor
not: issues cards to consumers

cards.subject: Tokenisation
says: replaces card details with a surrogate value
lets the merchant keep a reference instead of the card number
leaves the real number in the provider's secure vault
cards.use: need to charge a returning customer without storing card numbers
not: encrypts the number so the merchant can decrypt it later

cards.subject: A payment intent
says: represents one attempt to collect a specific amount
is created on the server before the customer pays
tracks the payment through states such as requires action and succeeded
cards.use: need one object to follow a payment through authentication and confirmation
not: is created again for every retry of the same sale

cards.subject: Hosted checkout
says: sends the customer to a page run by the provider
keeps card entry off the merchant's own servers
gives the quickest route to accepting cards safely
cards.use: want the least card-data exposure with the quickest integration
not: gives the merchant total control of the page layout

cards.subject: A direct API integration
says: collects card details on the merchant's own page and sends them to the API
widens the merchant's PCI scope
gives full control of the checkout design
cards.use: want complete control of the checkout and accept the compliance burden
not: keeps card numbers away from the merchant's servers

cards.subject: A merchant of record
says: is the party that acts as the legal seller to the customer
usually takes on the sales tax handling for the transaction
appears as the seller on the customer's receipt
cards.use: want a third party to act as the legal seller of your product
not: only forwards payments and never sells to the customer

cards.subject: An alternative payment method
says: covers wallets, bank transfers and direct debits as well as cards
has its own flow and failure modes
may confirm only after the customer has left the checkout
cards.use: need to offer customers choices other than cards
not: always settles instantly

cards.subject: A statement descriptor
says: is the text on the customer's bank statement for a charge
helps customers recognise a payment
reduces disputes from people who do not recognise a charge
cards.use: get disputes from customers who say they never made the payment but did
not: is a tax identifier printed on invoices

cards.subject: A direct debit
says: pulls money from the customer's bank account under a mandate
can be returned or disputed after the money has moved
suits regular payments that the customer authorises once
cards.use: collect regular payments straight from a bank account
not: is confirmed immediately in real time

cards.subject: A webhook
says: is an HTTP request the provider sends when an event happens
lets you learn about asynchronous outcomes without polling
arrives at an endpoint that you expose
cards.use: need to learn when a payment finally succeeds after the customer has left
not: is a request your server makes to the provider on a timer

cards.subject: Polling
says: asks the provider repeatedly for the current state
adds delay and request load
can repair a webhook that was missed
cards.use: need a fallback because a webhook may never have arrived
not: tells you about changes the instant they happen

cards.subject: Signature verification
says: proves a webhook really came from the provider
computes a hash over the raw body with a shared secret
must pass before the payload is trusted
cards.use: worry that anyone can post fake payment events to your endpoint
not: is unnecessary when the endpoint URL is secret

cards.subject: An idempotency key
says: lets a repeated request return the original result
is a unique value the client sends with a write request
stops a retry from charging twice
cards.use: want to retry a charge after a network timeout without double charging
not: is stored by the receiving side of a webhook to skip repeats

cards.subject: Event-id deduplication
says: stores the ids of events already processed
makes a handler safe when the same event arrives twice
runs on the receiving side of a webhook
cards.use: get the same webhook delivered more than once
not: is sent by the client with a write request

cards.subject: At-least-once delivery
says: may deliver the same event more than once
retries until the endpoint acknowledges
forces consumers to be idempotent
cards.use: design a handler for a provider that retries on any non-2xx response
not: guarantees each event arrives exactly once

cards.subject: Fast acknowledgement
says: returns a 2xx quickly and does the work afterwards
avoids timeouts that trigger redelivery
usually hands the event to a queue
cards.use: have a webhook handler doing slow work inline
not: waits for the entire business process before replying

cards.subject: Out-of-order delivery
says: can deliver a later event before an earlier one
makes handlers fetch current state or compare timestamps
breaks code that assumes a fixed event sequence
cards.use: find a refund event arriving before the payment it refers to
not: is prevented by at-least-once delivery

cards.subject: A dead-letter queue
says: holds events that failed after all retries
lets people inspect and replay failures
stops one poison message blocking the rest
cards.use: must not lose events that keep failing processing
not: silently discards failed events

cards.subject: Key reuse with different parameters
says: should be rejected as a conflict
signals a client bug that mutates a retried request
must not return the result of the earlier, different request
cards.use: see the same idempotency key arrive with a changed amount
not: is safe because the newest parameters simply win

cards.subject: Double entry
says: records every transaction as equal debits and credits
keeps the books balanced by design
moves value between accounts rather than creating it
cards.use: want every movement of money to leave a balanced trail
not: records each transaction on one account only

cards.subject: A debit entry
says: sits on the left side of a posting
increases asset and expense accounts
decreases liability and income accounts
cards.use: ask which side increases an asset account
not: always means money leaving the business

cards.subject: A credit entry
says: sits on the right side of a posting
increases liability, equity and income accounts
decreases asset accounts
cards.use: ask which side increases a liability or income account
not: always means money coming into the business

cards.subject: A journal entry
says: is one posted transaction made of two or more lines
has total debits equal to total credits
carries a date and a description
cards.use: need to post a movement across several accounts
not: can be saved with unequal totals if flagged

cards.subject: A chart of accounts
says: lists every account the ledger can post to
groups accounts into assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses
is the structure that reports are built from
cards.use: need to decide which accounts a new type of transaction posts to
not: holds the individual customer invoices

cards.subject: A trial balance
says: lists the balance of every account
shows total debits equal to total credits when postings balance
checks balance, not correctness
cards.use: want a quick check that postings are balanced
not: proves every posting went to the right account

cards.subject: A reversing entry
says: corrects an error by posting the opposite of the original
leaves the original entry visible
is how an append-only ledger fixes mistakes
cards.use: find a wrong posting that must be undone
not: deletes the original posting from the ledger

cards.subject: Append-only posting
says: never edits or deletes a posted entry
keeps a complete audit trail
uses new entries to make corrections
cards.use: must show auditors what happened and when
not: allows posted entries to be edited if the user has permission

cards.subject: Accounts receivable
says: is money that customers owe the business
is an asset
is cleared when the customer pays
cards.use: ask where an unpaid sent invoice sits in the books
not: is money the business owes its suppliers

cards.subject: Deferred revenue
says: is cash received for service not yet delivered
is held as a liability until earned
is released to revenue as the service period passes
cards.use: bill a customer for a whole year in advance
not: counts as earned revenue the moment cash arrives

cards.subject: A clearing account
says: holds money in transit between systems
should return to zero once items are matched
signals unmatched items when its balance lingers
cards.use: need to book provider payments before the bank shows the money
not: permanently stores the profit of the business

cards.subject: An invoice
says: requests payment for goods or services delivered
lists lines, quantities and amounts
creates a receivable when issued
cards.use: need to ask a customer for payment
not: is proof that payment has already been received

cards.subject: The invoice lifecycle
says: moves from draft to sent to paid
can pass through a part paid state
can end as void instead of paid
cards.use: ask what states an invoice can be in
not: lets a sent invoice return to draft and be edited freely

cards.subject: A credit note
says: reverses some or all of an invoice
carries its own number linked to the original
leaves the original invoice intact
cards.use: need to correct a sent invoice without deleting it
not: is used to request extra payment

cards.subject: A void invoice
says: cancels an invoice that should not stand at all
keeps its number in the sequence
is used when nothing at all is due
cards.use: issued an invoice by mistake and nothing is owed
not: removes its number so the sequence is closed up

cards.subject: Sequential invoice numbering
says: gives every invoice a unique number in order
makes gaps visible to auditors
is why sent invoices are voided or credited, never deleted
cards.use: must show that no invoice has silently disappeared
not: is optional and numbers can be reused

cards.subject: A partial payment
says: pays only part of an invoice
leaves the remaining balance open
has to be allocated to the right invoice
cards.use: receive less than the invoice total
not: closes the invoice as paid

cards.subject: Payment allocation
says: matches received money to specific invoices
must cope with one payment covering many invoices
stops the same money paying two invoices
cards.use: receive a single bank transfer for several invoices
not: is done automatically by the bank

cards.subject: Account credit
says: keeps unused money on the customer's account
offsets future invoices
is not a refund to the card
cards.use: owe a customer money but they will keep buying
not: must always be paid out in cash

cards.subject: An invoice snapshot
says: freezes prices, tax and customer details at issue time
stops later catalogue changes rewriting history
is what the customer sees if they download it again later
cards.use: change a product's details after invoices have been issued
not: updates every old invoice when the catalogue changes

cards.subject: An idempotent refund
says: carries a unique key on every refund request
refuses to refund more than was paid in total
survives provider retries and staff double-clicks
cards.use: worry that a double-click could refund the same payment twice
not: relies on staff remembering what they already refunded

cards.subject: A subscription
says: links a customer to a plan for repeating billing periods
bills automatically each period
has a status such as active or cancelled
cards.use: sell something that renews on a schedule
not: is a one-off charge with no renewal

cards.subject: A plan
says: defines the recurring product, interval and entitlements
can be changed by moving a subscription to another plan
is what a customer chooses at sign-up
cards.use: describe what a customer buys each period
not: records each payment a customer has made

cards.subject: A billing period
says: is the interval between recurring invoices
has a start date and an end date
sets the window in which entitlements or usage are counted
cards.use: need to know which dates a charge covers
not: is the time a card authorisation stays valid

cards.subject: Proration
says: charges or credits for part of a period
applies when a plan changes mid-cycle
is computed from the time remaining
cards.use: upgrade a customer halfway through the month
not: bills the full new price from the original period start regardless

cards.subject: A free trial
says: gives access before the first charge
converts to paid at the end unless cancelled
may or may not require a payment method up front
cards.use: let a customer try a service before paying
not: is billed in full on day one then refunded

cards.subject: An entitlement
says: states what the plan lets the customer do
is kept apart from the money movement
should have exactly one owning service
cards.use: decide what a paying customer may use
not: is the invoice raised for the plan

cards.subject: Metered billing
says: charges for measured consumption
needs durable usage events
normally bills after the period has ended
cards.use: charge by how much a customer actually used
not: charges a flat amount whatever the usage

cards.subject: Billing in advance
says: charges at the start of the period
creates deferred revenue until the service is delivered
is the usual pattern for flat plans
cards.use: charge a flat plan before the service period begins
not: leaves the supplier carrying the risk of non-payment after delivery

cards.subject: Billing in arrears
says: charges after the period has ended
suits usage that is only known afterwards
leaves the supplier carrying credit risk
cards.use: charge for usage that can only be counted at period end
not: collects money before any service is delivered

cards.subject: Overage
says: is usage beyond the included allowance
can be blocked, throttled or billed
needs a policy decided in advance
cards.use: find customers using more than their plan includes
not: is a refund for unused allowance

cards.subject: Cancellation at period end
says: keeps access until the paid period finishes
stops the next renewal
does not refund the current period
cards.use: let a customer leave but keep what they already paid for
not: ends access and refunds immediately

cards.subject: A subscription state machine
says: has states such as trialling, active, past due and cancelled
moves on events rather than manual edits
decides whether a customer with a failed payment keeps access
cards.use: need clear rules for what access each status gives
not: lets staff set any status directly at any time

cards.subject: Dunning
says: is the process of recovering failed or overdue payments
combines reminders with retries
aims to keep the customer rather than punish them
cards.use: want to recover renewals that failed to charge
not: is the process of issuing refunds in bulk

cards.subject: A payment retry schedule
says: re-attempts a failed charge at planned intervals
recovers payments whose cause was temporary
stops after a defined limit
cards.use: want failed renewals to be tried again automatically
not: retries instantly and indefinitely

cards.subject: A soft decline
says: is a failure that may succeed later, such as insufficient funds
justifies a scheduled retry
may clear after the customer tops up or a limit resets
cards.use: see a renewal fail for a temporary reason
not: is a permanent refusal that retries cannot fix

cards.subject: A hard decline
says: is a permanent refusal such as a closed account
should not be retried blindly
needs the customer to supply a new payment method
cards.use: see an issuer report the card as closed or stolen
not: is worth retrying every hour

cards.subject: A card account updater
says: refreshes expired or reissued card details automatically
reduces failures caused by card replacement
works through the card networks and issuers
cards.use: lose renewals because customers' cards were replaced
not: is a manual spreadsheet that staff keep

cards.subject: A grace period
says: keeps access for a set time after a failed payment
gives retries time to succeed
ends in suspension or cancellation if unpaid
cards.use: want a customer to keep working while a card issue is fixed
not: cancels access the moment a payment fails

cards.subject: The past-due status
says: marks a subscription whose latest invoice is unpaid
sits between active and cancelled
still allows recovery
cards.use: ask what to call a subscription with an unpaid renewal
not: means the subscription has already been cancelled

cards.subject: Involuntary churn
says: is customer loss caused by failed payments
is reduced by retries and card updaters
should be measured apart from voluntary cancellation
cards.use: lose subscribers who never chose to leave
not: is counted as customers who cancelled on purpose

cards.subject: A write-off
says: removes an uncollectable invoice from receivables
is booked as bad debt expense
needs an approval and a reason
cards.use: conclude that an overdue invoice will never be paid
not: silently deletes the invoice record

cards.subject: VAT
says: is charged on sales at each stage of a supply chain
is collected by the seller and passed to the tax authority
lets a registered buyer set input tax against output tax
cards.use: ask how a sales tax that applies at every stage works
not: is paid only by the final consumer's bank

cards.subject: Output tax
says: is tax charged on your own sales
is owed to the tax authority
is netted against input tax in a return
cards.use: need the tax collected from customers on a sale
not: is tax paid on your own purchases

cards.subject: Input tax
says: is tax paid on your own purchases
may be offset against output tax when recoverable
depends on the nature of the purchase
cards.use: need the tax you were charged by suppliers
not: is tax you charge your customers

cards.subject: A tax-exclusive price
says: shows the amount before tax is added
shows tax as a separate line
is the usual way to quote to businesses
cards.use: quote a price to a business buyer who will reclaim tax
not: already contains the tax in the total

cards.subject: A tax-inclusive price
says: shows a total that already contains tax
needs the tax part extracted by calculation
is the usual way to show prices to consumers
cards.use: show consumers a price they will actually pay
not: adds tax on top at the till

cards.subject: An effective-dated tax rate
says: keeps old rates for old transactions
applies the rate valid on the supply date
stops a rate change rewriting history
cards.use: find that a tax rate changed halfway through a billing year
not: overwrites the old rate in place

cards.subject: The reverse charge
says: shifts responsibility for reporting the tax to the buyer
shows no tax charged on the supplier's invoice
applies to certain cross-border business sales
cards.use: sell to a business customer in another country under special rules
not: makes the supplier collect extra tax

cards.subject: Place of supply
says: decides which jurisdiction's tax rules apply
often depends on the customer's location for digital services
is why evidence of customer location is kept
cards.use: sell a digital service to customers in several countries
not: is always where the seller is registered

cards.subject: Tax on a credit note
says: reverses the tax originally charged
affects the return for the period in which it is issued
follows the invoice it credits
cards.use: issue a credit note for a taxed invoice
not: is ignored by the tax return

cards.subject: A zero-rated supply
says: is taxable at a rate of zero percent
still counts as a taxable sale on returns
can allow related input tax to be recovered
cards.use: sell something taxable at a nil rate
not: falls outside the tax system completely

cards.subject: An exempt supply
says: falls outside charging tax
usually restricts recovery of related input tax
is not simply taxed at zero
cards.use: sell something the tax rules exempt
not: always allows full recovery of input tax

cards.subject: PCI-DSS
says: is a security standard for organisations handling card data
is maintained by an industry council rather than a government
applies to anyone who stores, processes or transmits card data
cards.use: ask what security standard applies to taking card payments
not: is a law passed by a national parliament

cards.subject: Cardholder data
says: includes the primary account number
is what the standard exists to protect
becomes more sensitive when stored with the name and expiry
cards.use: ask what information PCI-DSS is protecting
not: is only the customer's email address

cards.subject: Sensitive authentication data
says: includes the card security code
must never be stored after authorisation
stays prohibited even when encrypted
cards.use: wonder whether you may keep the card security code for later charges
not: may be stored if it is encrypted

cards.subject: PCI scope
says: is the set of systems that touch card data
shrinks when card entry is outsourced
drives the amount of compliance work
cards.use: want to reduce your compliance workload
not: covers only the payment page and nothing else

cards.subject: Hosted fields
says: show provider-hosted inputs inside your own page
keep card numbers from touching your servers
allow a custom look with less scope
cards.use: want a branded card form without handling card numbers
not: send card numbers through your server before the provider

cards.subject: Velocity checks
says: limit how many attempts occur in a time window
catch card testing and credential stuffing
can be applied per card, per IP or per account
cards.use: see many payment attempts arriving in seconds
not: verify the address on the card

cards.subject: Card testing
says: is the use of small attempts to find which stolen numbers work
tends to produce many small declined payments
is slowed by velocity limits and bot challenges
cards.use: see a burst of tiny failed payments with different card numbers
not: is a legitimate load test run by the issuer

cards.subject: A fraud risk score
says: combines many signals into one likelihood figure
lets rules allow, review or block
needs tuning against real outcomes
cards.use: want to decide automatically which orders to review
not: is a guarantee that an order is genuine

cards.subject: Friendly fraud
says: is a dispute where the cardholder did make the purchase
is countered with delivery and usage evidence
is also called first-party misuse
cards.use: get a chargeback for something the customer actually received
not: is fraud by a stranger using stolen card details

cards.subject: Account takeover
says: is an attacker using a real customer's credentials
is slowed by multi-factor authentication
can lead to stored payment methods being misused
cards.use: see a real customer's account used from a new device to buy
not: is when a company buys another company's accounts

cards.subject: The chargeback ratio
says: compares disputes to the number of transactions
can trigger monitoring programmes if it stays high
is improved by clear descriptors and prompt refunds
cards.use: watch disputes climb relative to sales
not: compares refunds to authorisations only

cards.subject: Reconciliation
says: compares your records with an outside source
investigates the differences it finds
should run on a schedule rather than only when something looks wrong
cards.use: want to know whether your books agree with the bank
not: edits the ledger until it matches

cards.subject: Bank reconciliation
says: matches ledger entries to bank statement lines
finds missing, extra and mismatched items
ends with explained differences
cards.use: need to check the ledger's cash against the bank statement
not: compares two internal reports from the same system

cards.subject: A settlement report
says: lists the payments, fees and refunds inside each payout
is what you match to a bank deposit
comes from the provider
cards.use: want to see what is inside a payout
not: is the cardholder's statement

cards.subject: Payout reconciliation
says: matches one bank deposit to the transactions it contained
explains why a deposit differs from the sum of charges
needs the provider's per-payout detail
cards.use: find a deposit that is smaller than the day's sales
not: matches the bank statement to supplier bills

cards.subject: A timing difference
says: is a gap that closes by itself as items clear
is not an error
appears when a payment is recorded before the bank shows it
cards.use: see an item in the ledger that the bank has not yet shown
not: is a permanent error that needs a reversal

cards.subject: An unmatched item
says: has no counterpart in the other source
must be investigated and owned
becomes riskier as it ages
cards.use: find a bank line with no matching ledger entry
not: is a duplicate that can be deleted at once

cards.subject: Duplicate detection
says: recognises the same transaction arriving by two routes
makes repeated imports safe
compares details such as reference, amount and date
cards.use: import a bank file that overlaps with one already loaded
not: posts every imported line as new

cards.subject: A suspense account
says: holds items that cannot yet be identified
should be cleared quickly
signals a problem when its balance grows
cards.use: receive money you cannot yet attribute to a customer
not: is the account where profit is retained

cards.subject: A stale approval
says: no longer counts once the underlying figures change
is detected by comparing a fingerprint of the figures
means the figures must be put up again
cards.use: find that data changed after sign-off
not: remains valid because it was once given

cards.subject: Minor units
says: store amounts as whole numbers of the smallest currency unit
avoid decimal fractions in storage
are how pence or cents are held as integers
cards.use: must store an amount like 19.99 pounds exactly
not: store amounts as floating-point numbers

cards.subject: An ISO 4217 code
says: identifies a currency with three letters
must accompany every stored amount
includes codes such as GBP and EUR
cards.use: need an unambiguous name for a currency
not: identifies a country rather than a currency

cards.subject: Floating-point arithmetic
says: cannot represent many decimal fractions exactly
is why 0.1 plus 0.2 does not equal 0.3 exactly
should not carry money values
cards.use: are tempted to use a float for a price
not: is exact for any decimal value

cards.subject: A decimal type
says: stores exact base-10 numbers
suits values with fractions of a minor unit
avoids binary rounding surprises
cards.use: need exact decimals such as an exchange rate
not: is stored as a binary float

cards.subject: The currency exponent
says: differs between currencies
is zero for some currencies and three for others
is why two decimals must not be hard-coded
cards.use: handle a currency that has no minor unit
not: is always two for every currency

cards.subject: A rounding policy
says: decides how fractions of a minor unit are resolved
should be chosen once and applied consistently
states where in the calculation rounding happens
cards.use: find invoice totals that differ by a penny from the sum of the lines
not: is decided separately by each developer on each screen

cards.subject: Remainder allocation
says: splits an amount without losing or creating a minor unit
gives leftover units to chosen parts
makes the parts add up to the whole
cards.use: need to split 100 pence across three payees
not: rounds each share and ignores the difference

cards.subject: An exchange-rate snapshot
says: stores the rate used at the time of the transaction
makes later reporting reproducible
is kept with the document it was used for
cards.use: must explain a converted amount months later
not: looks up today's rate each time a report is run

cards.subject: Presentment currency
says: is the currency shown to the customer
may differ from the settlement currency
is chosen to make pricing familiar
cards.use: show customers prices in their own currency
not: is the currency of the merchant's bank deposit

cards.subject: Settlement currency
says: is the currency in which funds reach the merchant
may require conversion from the presentment currency
is fixed by the merchant's account setup
cards.use: ask in which currency the bank deposit arrives
not: is the currency printed on the customer's receipt

cards.subject: An FX gain or loss
says: arises when rates move between invoice and payment
is booked as its own ledger line
is separate from the sale's revenue
cards.use: receive a foreign-currency payment worth a different amount than invoiced
not: is added silently to revenue

cards.subject: A payout
says: sends collected funds from the provider to the merchant's bank
arrives as a net amount
follows a schedule
cards.use: want to know how collected funds reach your bank account
not: refunds money to the customer's card

cards.subject: A payout schedule
says: sets how often the balance is transferred
adds a delay after capture
may be daily, weekly or monthly
cards.use: need to know when funds will reach the bank
not: is set by the customer at checkout

cards.subject: A reserve
says: withholds part of the balance against future refunds and disputes
is based on risk
is released later
cards.use: see a provider hold back part of the balance
not: is a fee deducted for good

cards.subject: A negative balance
says: arises when refunds and disputes exceed available funds
must be covered by the merchant
can be recovered from future payments
cards.use: issue refunds greater than the balance in the account
not: is a credit the provider gives the merchant

cards.subject: A split payment
says: divides one customer payment between platform and sellers
needs the share of each party recorded
is common in marketplaces
cards.use: run a marketplace where a customer pays several sellers at once
not: sends the entire amount to the platform's account only

cards.subject: A connected account
says: is a seller account that sits under a platform
receives its share of marketplace payments
goes through onboarding checks
cards.use: need each seller to be paid separately by a platform
not: is the platform's own bank account

cards.subject: KYC onboarding
says: verifies the identity of a seller before payouts
is required before funds can be sent out
may need documents such as proof of identity
cards.use: onboard a seller who will receive money
not: is a fraud check on each buyer's card

cards.subject: A sandbox
says: simulates the provider without moving real money
uses separate API keys and data
behaves like live in most but not all ways
cards.use: want to build an integration without risking real money
not: charges real cards at a discount

cards.subject: Live mode
says: moves real money
uses its own live keys
needs real accounts and verified settings
cards.use: are ready to accept real payments
not: accepts only test card numbers

cards.subject: A test card number
says: is a published number that triggers a specific outcome in the sandbox
fails in live mode
can simulate declines and authentication
cards.use: need to see what happens when a card is declined
not: works to make real purchases

cards.subject: A secret API key
says: must never be shipped to browsers or mobile apps
authorises server-side calls
is kept in server configuration
cards.use: configure a server that calls the provider
not: is safe to publish in front-end code

cards.subject: A publishable key
says: may appear in browser code
identifies the account to the client library
cannot perform privileged server actions
cards.use: initialise the provider's client library on a web page
not: must be hidden like a password

cards.subject: A sandbox parity gap
says: means passing in the sandbox does not prove live behaviour
comes from differences such as speed, rules and bank behaviour
is why a small live check is done
cards.use: find a flow that worked in testing but failed with real banks
not: is impossible because the sandbox copies live exactly

cards.subject: A live smoke test
says: runs one small real transaction after launch
is followed by a refund or void
confirms keys, webhooks and payouts are wired
cards.use: want proof that live configuration works before announcing it
not: replaces all sandbox testing

cards.subject: A test clock
says: advances simulated time for subscriptions
lets you test renewals and trials without waiting
exists only in the test environment
cards.use: need to test a month-end renewal today
not: changes the date on the production server

cards.subject: ggmoney
says: is a plain-PHP bookkeeping tool
is built around UK HMRC filing
posts invoices and bills into a double-entry ledger
cards.use: ask which bookkeeping tool is built around HMRC filing
not: is a hosted card-payments processor

cards.subject: The ggmoney ledger
says: has a chart of accounts and journals
reads performance report actuals directly
keeps one source of truth rather than a separate copy
cards.use: ask where ggmoney performance figures come from
not: feeds reports from a duplicate reporting table

cards.subject: Moving a ledger line to another brand
says: changes only the brand tag
never changes the amount
keeps the history of the original posting
cards.use: need to move older lines onto a different brand in ggmoney
not: recalculates the amounts for the new brand

cards.subject: The ggmoney banking layer
says: reads transactions through read-only Open Banking feeds or CSV import
cannot move money
feeds reconciliation with outside evidence
cards.use: ask how ggmoney gets bank transactions
not: initiates payments from the bank account

cards.subject: ggmoney import matching
says: recognises a transaction that arrives by feed and CSV as one
makes imports safe to repeat
stops a double import inflating cash
cards.use: worry that importing a CSV after a feed will double-count
not: posts both copies and asks staff to delete one

cards.subject: A ggmoney performance review
says: freezes a period's figures with a fingerprint
is approved by someone other than the preparer
goes stale if the ledger moves first
cards.use: need performance figures signed off in ggmoney
not: stays approved even after the ledger changes

cards.subject: The Moksy subscriptions service
says: owns plan entitlements and the current billing period
holds included monthly tokens and consumed tokens
holds the overage posture
cards.use: ask which Moksy service owns entitlements
not: is the source of truth for checkout transactions

cards.subject: The Moksy payments service
says: stays the source of truth for money movement, invoices and payouts
owns checkout transactions
does not own plan entitlements
cards.use: ask which Moksy service owns invoices and payouts
not: is the authoritative owner of consumed tokens

cards.subject: The Moksy token ledger
says: records a durable usage event for every AI request
is the event log that the snapshot summarises
is the source from which usage is counted
cards.use: ask where Moksy records AI usage
not: keeps only a running total with no events

cards.subject: The Moksy usage snapshot
says: is a fast-read summary of the current period
is derived from the usage events
is only a summary, not the source of truth
cards.use: need a quick read of current-period consumption
not: replaces the event log as the record

cards.subject: Moksy allowance enforcement
says: is designed with three modes: block, downgrade or bill overage
is described in the design for when the allowance runs out
is a later phase of the rollout
cards.use: ask what happens when a Moksy plan's tokens run out
not: is already marked as implemented in the rollout document

cards.subject: The Moksy billing rollout plan
says: marks the foundation phase as implemented
lists enforcement as a later phase
lists invoices from the token ledger as a later phase
cards.use: must say what is built and what is planned in Moksy billing
not: says every billing phase is already built

cards.subject: Moksy token reconciliation
says: is planned to compare provider invoices with the token ledger
is planned to detect missing or duplicated usage events
is described as planned rather than built
cards.use: ask how Moksy plans to check AI usage against provider bills
not: is already running in production

qa.q: What does a card authorisation do?
qa.right: Asks the issuer to approve the payment and hold the funds
wrong: Transfers the money to the merchant's bank straight away
Creates an invoice for the order
qa.why: An authorisation reserves funds; capture and settlement move them later.

qa.q: Why is money usually stored as integers of the smallest currency unit?
qa.right: To avoid floating-point rounding errors
wrong: Because databases cannot store decimal numbers
Because it removes the need for currency codes
qa.why: Whole numbers of minor units are exact; binary floats cannot represent many decimals.

qa.q: In double-entry bookkeeping, what must be true of every journal entry?
qa.right: Total debits equal total credits
wrong: It is always posted to the bank account
It has a positive total on the debit side only
qa.why: Balanced debits and credits are the defining rule of double entry.

qa.q: What is a webhook?
qa.right: An HTTP request the provider sends to your endpoint when an event happens
wrong: A request your server sends to the provider every minute
A browser plug-in that fills in card forms
A report the bank emails each month
qa.why: Webhooks push event notifications to a URL you expose.

qa.q: What is a chargeback?
qa.right: A dispute raised by the cardholder with their issuer that pulls the amount back pending the outcome
wrong: A refund the merchant chooses to give
A fee charged for failed payments
A second authorisation of the same card
qa.why: Chargebacks start at the cardholder's bank, not with the merchant.

qa.q: What does PCI-DSS cover?
qa.right: Security requirements for organisations that store, process or transmit card data
wrong: Rules on how invoices must be numbered
qa.why: It is an industry security standard for card data.

qa.q: What is a sandbox environment for?
qa.right: Testing an integration without moving real money
wrong: Storing live customer cards for later
qa.why: Sandboxes use separate keys and data and simulate the provider.

qa.q: A client sends the request below and the network drops before it sees the reply. It retries with the same header. What should a well-designed API do?
qa.right: Return the result of the first request without charging again
wrong: Create a second charge because every request is new
Reject all retries for a day
Charge half the amount on the retry
qa.why: The idempotency key lets the server recognise a repeat and replay the first outcome.

qa.q: What is the difference between a void and a refund?
qa.right: A void cancels before capture so no money moves; a refund returns money that was captured
wrong: A void is for chargebacks and a refund is for fraud
A void is always partial and a refund is always full
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
qa.why: Voids release a hold; refunds reverse a completed capture.

qa.q: What does this print in most programming languages that use binary floating point?
qa.why: 0.1 and 0.2 are not exactly representable, so the sum carries a tiny error.

qa.q: A price shown as 120 includes tax at a rate of 20 percent. How much of the 120 is tax?
qa.why: Net is 120 divided by 1.2, which is 100, so tax is 20.

qa.q: An invoice for 100 has received a payment of 60. Which status describes it best?
qa.right: Part paid
qa.why: A partial payment leaves a balance open.

qa.q: Why must a webhook signature be verified before the payload is trusted?
qa.right: Because anyone could post a fake event to a public endpoint
wrong: Because it makes the provider send fewer events
Because it speeds up the reply
Because unsigned events are always older
qa.why: The signature proves the sender knew the shared secret.

qa.q: What does proration do when a customer upgrades halfway through a billing period?
qa.right: Charges or credits only for the part of the period each plan applied
wrong: Charges the full new price and ignores the old plan
Cancels the subscription and creates a new customer
Waits until the next period to apply any change
qa.why: Proration works out amounts from the time remaining.

qa.q: Which identifier names a currency unambiguously in stored amounts?
qa.right: A three-letter ISO 4217 code such as GBP
qa.why: Symbols are ambiguous; codes are standard.

qa.q: Your webhook handler sends emails and builds PDFs inline and takes about ten seconds. The provider keeps redelivering events. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Acknowledge with a 2xx straight away and process the event from a queue, idempotently
wrong: Ask the provider for more retries
Turn off signature verification to save time
Ignore any event after the first delivery
qa.why: A fast acknowledgement stops timeouts; the queued work must still be safe to repeat.

qa.q: The same payment succeeded event arrives twice and your handler posts two ledger entries. What would have prevented this?
qa.right: Recording processed event ids and skipping events already handled
wrong: Sending an idempotency key to the provider
Switching the handler to polling every second
Posting entries with a rounding policy
qa.why: Event-id deduplication makes the receiving side safe under at-least-once delivery.

qa.q: A bank deposit is smaller than the sum of yesterday's charges. What should you check first?
qa.right: The settlement report for refunds, fees and disputes netted from the payout
wrong: Whether the currency code has three letters
Whether the ledger was double-counted by the bank
qa.why: Payouts are net of deductions that the settlement report itemises.

qa.q: A subscription renewal fails with an insufficient-funds decline. What is the sensible response?
qa.right: Treat it as a soft decline: retry on a schedule and tell the customer
wrong: Retry every minute until it works
qa.why: Temporary failures justify spaced retries with customer communication.

qa.q: An issuer reports the card as stolen. What should the billing system do?
qa.right: Treat it as a hard decline and ask for a new payment method
wrong: Wait for the customer to complain
qa.why: Permanent refusals will not succeed on retry.

qa.q: How should 100 pence be split across three payees without losing a penny?
qa.why: Remainder allocation hands leftover minor units to chosen parts so the total stays whole.

qa.q: A developer wants to log whole checkout request bodies, card fields included, to debug failures. What is the problem?
qa.right: Card data in logs pulls logs, backups and tools into PCI scope, so log ids and tokens instead
wrong: Logs are too slow to hold request bodies
Card numbers are public so logging them is harmless
qa.why: Keeping card data out of logs keeps scope small and risk low.

qa.q: A customer completes a bank prompt for 3-D Secure, then closes the tab. How do you learn the final outcome?
qa.right: Through a webhook for the payment's final state, with polling as a fallback
wrong: It is certain to be successful
By asking the customer to email
qa.why: Outcomes can finish after the customer has gone; the server must learn asynchronously.

qa.q: Which key may be placed in browser code?
qa.right: The publishable key
qa.why: Publishable keys identify the account but cannot perform privileged actions.

qa.q: What happens to VAT when you issue a credit note against a taxed invoice?
qa.right: The credit note reverses the tax and affects the return for the period it is issued
wrong: Nothing, because tax stays as originally charged
The tax is paid again in the original period
The tax moves into deferred revenue
qa.why: Tax follows the invoice and its credit note.

qa.q: A customer pays annually in advance. How should the supplier account for the cash on receipt?
qa.right: As deferred revenue, released to revenue over the service period
qa.why: Cash for undelivered service is a liability until earned.

qa.q: A team rounds each invoice line to two decimals, and totals sometimes differ by a penny from rounding the exact sum. What is the right fix?
qa.right: Define one rounding policy and apply it consistently, including who gets any remainder
wrong: Let each screen round however it likes
qa.why: Consistency, not a particular rule, is what makes totals reproducible.

qa.q: A refund event reaches your handler before the payment event it refers to. What is the best design?
qa.right: Make handlers tolerate order, for example by fetching current state or comparing timestamps
wrong: Assume the provider will fix the order
Hold all events for a day and sort them
qa.why: Webhooks can arrive out of order.

qa.q: Support staff double-click Refund and two refunds are created. Which controls prevent this?
qa.right: An idempotency key on the request and a cap on total refunded against the payment
qa.why: Idempotent refunds survive double-clicks and retries.

qa.q: A team tests month-end renewals by editing period dates in the production database. What is better?
qa.right: Use a test clock in the sandbox to advance simulated time
wrong: Wait until the real month end
Edit the dates in the live provider dashboard
qa.why: Test clocks let you simulate time without touching live data.

qa.q: Everything passed in the sandbox, but on launch day payments from one type of card fail. What practice would have caught this?
qa.right: A small live smoke test and awareness of the sandbox parity gap
qa.why: The sandbox does not copy every real bank and card behaviour.

qa.q: A clearing account used for provider payments has shown a growing balance for three months. What does that most likely mean?
qa.right: Items are not being matched and cleared out
wrong: The chart of accounts is too small
qa.why: A clearing account should return to zero once items match.

qa.q: A month's figures were approved, then a back-dated entry changed them. What should happen to the approval?
qa.right: It goes stale and the figures are put up for approval again
wrong: It remains valid because it was given in good faith
It is deleted along with the entry
qa.why: Approval applies to the figures as they were; changed figures need fresh approval.

qa.q: A customer disputes a charge claiming non-delivery, and you hold courier proof of delivery. What is the right step?
qa.right: Submit the evidence as representment before the deadline
wrong: Issue a refund and ignore the dispute
Wait to see if the bank decides unprompted
qa.why: Chargebacks have a response deadline; evidence is submitted through the acquirer.

qa.q: Your chargeback ratio is climbing. What is the most useful first step?
qa.right: Segment the disputes by reason to see whether fraud, confusion or fulfilment is the cause
qa.why: Different causes need different fixes.

qa.q: A business sells a digital service to consumers in several countries. What mainly decides which tax rules apply?
qa.right: The place of supply, supported by evidence of the customer's location
wrong: The day of the week of the sale
qa.why: Place-of-supply rules often follow the customer's location.

qa.q: In Moksy's billing design, which service is the authoritative owner of plan entitlements?
qa.right: The subscriptions service
qa.why: The payments service owns money movement, not entitlements.

qa.q: In Moksy's design, if the usage snapshot and the token event log disagree, which is the record?
qa.right: The token ledger event log
qa.why: The event log is the ledger; the snapshot is only a summary.

qa.q: Two services both store a customer's plan entitlements and they now disagree. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Give each fact one owning service and derive the other copy from it
wrong: Add a nightly job that picks the newer copy
Store the entitlement in a third service as well
Let staff correct whichever looks wrong
qa.why: Facts stored in two places drift; one owner prevents that.

qa.q: Many small payments of low value, each with a different card number, arrive from one IP address in a minute. What is likely happening and what helps?
qa.right: Card testing; velocity limits and bot challenges help
wrong: A normal sales rush; do nothing
A currency mismatch; round the amounts
qa.why: Bursts of tiny declined payments are the signature of card testing.

qa.q: An invoice has the wrong amount and has already been sent. What is the usual practice?
qa.right: Issue a credit note and a corrected invoice, keeping the original
wrong: Delete the invoice and reuse its number
Ignore the difference until year end
qa.why: The original stays intact and the sequence has no silent gaps.

qa.q: The ledger shows an invoice paid, but ggmoney imports the same bank line by feed and by CSV. What stops double-counting?
qa.right: Import matching that recognises it as one transaction
wrong: Deleting one of the lines by hand each month
Posting both and letting the totals offset
qa.why: Duplicate-safe import is part of ggmoney's banking layer.

qa.q: A platform's seller refunds exceed their balance. What results?
qa.right: A negative balance that has to be covered or recovered from future payments
wrong: The provider silently absorbs the amount
The customers must repay the difference
qa.why: Negative balances arise when refunds and disputes exceed available funds.

qa.q: A client reuses an idempotency key but changes the amount. What should a good API do?
qa.right: Reject it as a conflict rather than return the old result
wrong: Return the first result as if nothing changed
qa.why: A reused key with different parameters signals a client bug.

qa.q: A EUR invoice is booked in a GBP ledger and is paid later at a different rate. Where does the difference go?
qa.right: To a separate FX gain or loss line
qa.why: Rate movement between invoice and payment is its own ledger item.

qa.q: Which statement about Moksy billing is correct according to its rollout document?
qa.right: The foundation phase is implemented, while enforcement and token-ledger invoices are later phases
qa.why: Treat later phases as planned, not built.

qa.q: Events that keep failing after all retries pile up. What is the right handling?
qa.right: Park them in a dead-letter queue, fix the cause and replay them
wrong: Delete them to keep the queue clear
qa.why: Dead-letter queues preserve failures for inspection and replay.

qa.q: A customer downgrades mid-cycle and is owed money for the unused time, but will continue as a customer. What fits best?
qa.right: Put the amount on the account as credit to offset the next invoice
qa.why: Account credit offsets future invoices without a refund.

qa.q: A business wants a partner to act as the legal seller to customers and handle tax collection on its sales. Which model is that?
qa.right: Merchant of record
qa.why: The merchant of record is the seller to the customer.

qa.q: An overdue invoice is judged uncollectable. What is the correct treatment?
qa.right: Write it off as bad debt through an approved entry, keeping the invoice record
qa.why: Write-offs are posted and approved, never silent deletions.

qa.q: Which of these is the correct order of a normal card payment flow?
qa.right: Authorise, capture, settle
qa.why: Money is approved, claimed, then moved in a batch.

qa.q: A webhook handler returns 500 on one event. What is the typical provider behaviour?
qa.right: It retries delivery, so the handler must be idempotent
wrong: It never sends the event again
It switches to polling your server
It marks the payment as failed
qa.why: At-least-once delivery means retries and possible duplicates.

qa.q: A trial subscription ends and the customer has not cancelled. What should usually happen?
qa.right: It converts to paid and the first invoice is raised
wrong: The plan stays free for ever
qa.why: Trials convert at the end unless cancelled.

qa.q: A payment appears in the ledger on the 31st but the bank statement shows it on the 2nd. How should you treat this?
qa.right: As a timing difference that clears by itself, not an error
wrong: As a duplicate to be deleted
qa.why: Timing differences close when the item clears.

qa.q: Where should a refund's tax effect be recorded for a VAT-registered seller?
qa.right: On the credit note, reversing the tax originally charged
wrong: Nowhere; refunds have no tax effect
On the original invoice by editing it
qa.why: Tax follows the invoice and the credit note reverses it.
